findings.claim: All six world religions affirm that the universe has a divine origin.
findings.truth: Buddhism has no creator God and no creation story; the same takeaway then says so. Five of the six affirm a divine origin.
findings.evidence: spec Theme 2, Buddhist perspectives: 'Buddhists have no creation story and no concept of a creator God'; lesson's own Buddhism section

findings.claim: for 'Explain two beliefs' questions, focus on giving two distinct religious traditions...
findings.truth: 'Explain two beliefs' is another board's question wording. On this paper the 8-mark part asks candidates to explain views from two religious traditions with sources of authority.
findings.evidence: spec summary of assessment (2-hour written exam, 120 marks + 6 SPaG, four compulsory themes; 30 marks per theme as 2/5/8/15)

findings.claim: The Abortion Act 1967 made abortion legal in Great Britain ... up to 24 weeks of pregnancy.
findings.truth: The 1967 Act set no 24-week limit. Section 37 of the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Act 1990 amended s.1 of the 1967 Act and set the 24-week limit for the main ground.
findings.evidence: legislation.gov.uk, HFEA 1990 s.37: 'that the pregnancy has not exceeded its twenty-fourth week...'

findings.claim: Spelling, punctuation and grammar count for 5% of the 15-mark question.
findings.truth: SPaG is 5% of the sum of all AO1-AO2 marks, i.e. 12 marks across the qualification; this paper carries 6 SPaG marks on top of its 120, awarded on specified extended-writing questions. 5% of one 15-mark question would be 0.75 marks.
findings.evidence: spec SPaG statement (lines ~4346-4360) and the assessment summary (120 marks plus 6 for spelling, punctuation and grammar)

findings.claim: Dignity in Dying and 'Right to Choose' are the named non-religious organisations on this topic.
findings.truth: The spec names the Humanist 'Dignity in Dying' movement (with Peter Singer, Darwin, Dawkins, Hawking and Humanist Climate Action). 'Right to Choose' is a way of framing the abortion argument, not an organisation.

findings.claim: The Bhagavad Gita (2:12-13) teaches ... just as a person changes clothes, the soul moves from one body to another at death.
findings.truth: The changing-clothes simile is Bhagavad Gita 2:22. Verses 2:12-13 use the image of a person passing from childhood to youth to old age before passing to another body. Both verses are in the spec's cited range (2:12-13, 22, 27).
findings.evidence: Bhagavad Gita 2:22 ('as a person puts on new garments'); spec Hindu perspectives cites Bhagavad Gita 2: 12-13, 22, 27

findings.claim: Secular psychological research shows that ethical behaviour is shaped primarily by environment, relationships and social norms.
findings.truth: No source is given and the finding is not settled. The point works as an argument a non-religious person makes, not as a research result.
findings.evidence: no citable source; unverifiable appeal to research inside a model answer

findings.claim: Research on funeral satisfaction consistently finds that personalisation is the factor most linked to mourners feeling the ceremony was meaningful.
findings.truth: No such settled body of research is citable. The bullet repeats the argument already made two bullets above, so it can go.
findings.evidence: no citable source; unverifiable appeal to research inside a model answer

findings.claim: Student-facing prose and mark schemes name internal band labels ('Mastering-level answers', Mastering/Secure/Developing/Emerging ladders).
findings.truth: This paper has no 'Mastering' band, so the label means nothing to a student. Options: strip the ladder names from student-facing prose in this unit now, or leave the unit to the fleet-wide band-ladder relabel queue (178 ladders) so every subject changes in step. Recommendation: leave it to that queue.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section; retro programme band-ladder queue

findings.claim: Buddhist environmental ethics flows from the first precept ... The Lam Rim Buddhist Centre ... is actively engaged in environmental sustainability projects.
findings.truth: True as written, but the spec's own named exemplars for Buddhist environmental responsibility are Buddhist Action Month, Right Action and the second Precept. No edit needed; the first precept is still creditable.

findings.claim: In the UK, abortion has been legal (under certain conditions) since 1967.
findings.truth: Great Britain, not the whole UK: Northern Ireland was covered by different law until 2019. The collapsible one paragraph later says this, so no edit.

summary: Eight fixes across all four lessons: the 24-week abortion limit wrongly credited to the 1967 Act, a wrong SPaG claim, 'all six religions affirm a divine origin' against the spec's Buddhist content, a rival board's question wording, 'Right to Choose' called an organisation, a Bhagavad Gita verse mis-attribution and two invented research claims in mark schemes. Scripture, Catechism paragraphs, Qur'an references and every answer key checked out.
